sources.text:
Retired NYPD detective charged with murder in George Washington Bridge shooting of Con Ed worker: officials
A retired police officer was arrested after police say he shot and killed a New York City utility worker on the George Washington Bridge Tuesday, according to authorities.
The NYPD said Victor Romero, 62, of Haverstraw, faces a murder charge after he allegedly shot and killed Con Edison worker Koran Irvine, 46, of Valley Cottage.
It appeared to be a road rage attack involving the two Rockland County residents, the New York Post reported.
Romero previously worked as an NYPD detective. He left the force 25 years ago, according to the Post.
PREGNANT WOMAN DRIVING HOME FROM PRENATAL VISIT SHOT DURING ALLEGED ROAD RAGE ATTACK: POLICE
The shooting occurred at 7:18 p.m. Tuesday.
Irvine was driving on the bridge Tuesday evening when he was shot in his shoulder, crashed into a median on the bridge and was later pronounced dead at a hospital, Fox News Digital has confirmed.
“Police responded to a 911 call of a male shot on the outbound, upper level roadway of the George Washington Bridge,” the NYPD said.
When investigators arrived, the victim was discovered unconscious and unresponsive in the driver’s seat of a vehicle with a gunshot wound to the rear of the right shoulder.
The victim was taken to Englewood Hospital, where he died, police said.

Romero was driving in a black Range Rover at the time, according to the New York Daily News.

According to his social media, Irvine had just celebrated working for Con Edison for 20 years and posted about the accomplishment in September.
“We are heartbroken by the tragic loss of a member of the Con Edison family in this senseless act of violence,” Con Edison said in a statement, FOX 5 New York reported.
“Our deepest condolences go out to his family, friends, colleagues and everyone who knew and loved him.”

An online fundraiser for Irvine’s family said in part, “Koran was a man full of life, love, and dedication to the people who meant the most to him. His family was his world, and he worked hard every day to provide for and support his wife, Patricia, and their children, Lea and Hiro. He loved deeply, valued his relationships, and always strived to give his family the best life possible.”

sources.news_title: Victor Romero: 62-year-old retired NYPD detective arrested in Koran Irvine's road rage killing
sources.text:
Victor Romero: 62-year-old retired NYPD detective arrested in Koran Irvine's road rage killing
Victor Romero, 62, was taken into custody Wednesday in connection with the killing of Koran Irvine, 46, of Valley Cottage, New York.
A retired New York City police detective has been charged with murder in connection with the fatal shooting of a motorist during an apparent road rage incident on the George Washington Bridge.
Victor Romero, 62, was taken into custody Wednesday in connection with the killing of Koran Irvine, 46, of Valley Cottage, New York.
Motorist found shot on bridge
Irvine was found wounded and unconscious in the driver’s seat of a vehicle on the New Jersey-bound side of the bridge's upper level shortly after 7 p.m. Tuesday. He was taken to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead. Investigators later determined that he had been shot.
Police launched a search for a person of interest in the case. Romero was taken into custody at the NYPD’s 33rd Precinct, and officials confirmed Wednesday that he had been charged with murder.
Former detective retired in 2001
Romero, who lives in Haverstraw, New York, retired from the New York Police Department in 2001.
A phone number listed for him in public records went unanswered. Information about an attorney representing him was not immediately available.
Con Edison mourns employee
Irvine worked for Con Edison, the utility confirmed in a statement expressing grief over his death.
“We are heartbroken by the tragic loss of a member of the Con Edison family in this senseless act of violence,” read a statement from a Con Edison spokesperson. “Our deepest condolences go out to his family, friends, colleagues, and everyone who knew and loved him."
Bridge lanes reopened
The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, which operates the bridge, said the lanes closed following the shooting reopened about five hours later.
GoFundMe launched
A GoFundMe campaign described Irvine as a man “full of life, love, and dedication to the people who meant the most to him.” He is survived by his wife and two children.
Investigation ongoing
Authorities continue to investigate the circumstances leading up to the shooting. Further details about what triggered the alleged road rage incident have not been released.

sources.news_title: Retired NYPD detective faces murder charge in deadly George Washington Bridge shooting
sources.text:
Retired NYPD detective faces murder charge in deadly George Washington Bridge shooting
A retired NYPD detective is charged with murder in the deadly shooting on the George Washington Bridge Tuesday night, police said.
Victor Romero, 62, retired from the NYPD 25 years ago, police said. Police believe he fatally shot Koran Irvine in an apparent road rage incident.
Irvine, 46, was fatally shot just after 7 p.m. Tuesday night. Port Authority Police officers were responding to reports of a single-vehicle crash in the middle of the bridge and found Irvine with a gunshot wound. He was rushed to a nearby hospital where he later died.
Investigators have recovered a gun and it is being tested to determine if it is connected to the shooting. Romero's vehicle is in custody, police sources said. The NYPD is at Romero's home in Haverstraw, New York waiting to execute a search warrant, according to police sources.
Technology at the George Washington Bridge and license plate readers helped in the investigation.
Romero joined the NYPD in 1994. He worked for seven years and retired as a narcotics detective on disability after being shot by robbers at his family's coin laundry in Brooklyn.
In 2000, the Civilian Complaint Review Board received a complaint about Romero firing a weapon. Romero retired before the CCRB could complete its investigation.
Meanwhile, relatives have been gathering at Irvine's home in Valley Cottage in Rockland County.
"It's senseless. It's senseless," Irvine's friend Anthony Hodges said. "He became almost like a brother to me. He's just so vibrant. He always had a smile on his face. It was never a time I didn't have a conversation with him and he didn't smile. He was just such a lively person."
"He was a very nice man. We're new to the neighborhood. I remember when we first came, he would help us out. They have some chickens in the back. He brought us eggs to welcome us," neighbor Hope Dorcelly said. "I'm very shocked. We just heard about it this morning actually and we're just completely devastated for the family."
Irvine was married for 15 years to his wife Patricia, and has a teen girl and younger boy. In a statement posted on GoFundMe, the Irvine family said his "family was his world ... he loved deeply ... and always strived to give his family the best life possible."
Irvine was a 20-year employee of Con Edison.
"We are heartbroken by the tragic loss of a member of the Con Edison family in this senseless act of violence. Our deepest condolences go out to his family, friends, colleagues, and everyone who knew and loved him," the utility said in a statement.

sources.news_title: Retired NYPD Detective Held in Fatal George Washington Bridge Shooting
sources.text:
A retired NYPD detective was arrested Wednesday in connection with the fatal shooting of a married father of two on the George Washington Bridge, an apparent road-rage incident, police and sources said.
The former detective, who left the department 25 years ago, was taken into custody less than a day after Koran Irvine, 46, was shot in the right shoulder at about 7:15 p.m. Tuesday on the New Jersey-bound upper level of the bridge, according to sources.
Police had not publicly identified the suspect by late Wednesday afternoon. Charges were expected in connection with the shooting.
Investigators reviewing surveillance footage saw Irvine’s vehicle suddenly jolt as another car pulled alongside the rear passenger door. Sources said the movement may have captured the moment the shot was fired.
Irvine’s car then veered into the median and stopped, while the suspected shooter sped away, according to the sources.
NEXT UP: Cornell 7 Jane Doe Ends Suit Against Man Mistaken for Frat President
Investigators believe at this preliminary stage that one bullet was fired. The round pierced the rear window, grazed a headrest, struck Irvine’s right shoulder and exited through the left side of his neck, sources said.
Irvine was taken to Englewood Hospital, where he was later pronounced dead, authorities said.
The Valley Cottage, Rockland County, resident was the father of a son and daughter. Relatives also described him as deeply devoted to his wife and family.
“He’s a family man. Has always been a family man, and he lived his life 100% for his family, stayed out of trouble. And I am in disbelief at this point in time,” a cousin told The Post. “He was a man that lived for his family 100%, the only thing that he loved near and dear to his heart as much as his family was the Jets.”
Family members also remembered Irvine as a “jokester” who was always trying to make others laugh and feel good.
“He is always the light of the party,” the relative said. “He had so much life, was very attentive to everyone, always wanted to know people’s needs. He was so inviting.”

sources.news_title: George Washington Bridge Shooting: Con Ed Worker Killed
sources.text:
Con Edison worker Koran Irvine was fatally shot on the George Washington Bridge in an apparent road-rage attack, police say, and a person of interest has surrendered.
A 46-year-old father and longtime utility worker was gunned down during the evening commute on one of the busiest spans in the country, then pronounced dead after his car rolled into the median.
The Post reported that law enforcement sources tied the killing to a sudden burst of road rage on the New Jersey-bound upper level around 7:15 p.m. Tuesday. Police identified the slain driver as Koran Irvine of Valley Cottage in Rockland County. A person of interest turned himself in less than 24 hours later and was being questioned Wednesday afternoon.
Irvine had recently marked 20 years with Con Edison. Kin said he often picked up extra shifts and was scheduled to work overtime the next day. Instead, his family was left mourning a husband and dad described as the steady center of their home.
Investigators reviewing video described a tight, ugly sequence. Both motorists entered the upper level. Irvine appeared to swerve slightly toward the other car. That vehicle, apparently a dark-colored sedan, veered back into the middle lane.
The other driver then pulled up on the rear passenger side of Irvine’s car. Irvine’s ride suddenly jerked, the moment police believe the shot was fired, before rolling into the median and stopping. The suspect drove off.
Authorities preliminarily believe a single round was fired. The bullet pierced the back window, grazed the head rest, entered Irvine’s right shoulder, and exited the left side of his neck. He was rushed to Englewood Hospital and later pronounced dead.
No charges had been announced when the person of interest was being questioned. Police had not publicly named that individual, and it was not immediately clear whether anyone else was in the sedan.
Loved ones did not cast Irvine as a hard-edged road warrior. They described a devoted husband, a hands-on father, and a man who stayed out of trouble.
A cousin who would not give a name told reporters Wednesday what kind of man they lost.
"He’s a family man. Has always been a family man, and he lived his life 100% for his family, stayed out of trouble. And I am in disbelief at this point in time."
The same cousin added that almost nothing competed with that loyalty.
"He was a man that lived for his family 100%, the only thing that he loved near and dear to his heart as much as his family was the Jets."
Another relative, also unidentified, said the marriage itself was obvious to anyone who spent time around the couple.
"From just their dynamic and how you would experience it in person, you just felt that love in the air. They really loved each other. They were a special couple."
The kids felt it too. The relative said it had not been long since the family celebrated Irvine’s birthday, and that he filled a room on purpose.
"In his presence you were always laughing because he had such a positive vibe. He was always the light and he was always very loud but in a good way."
Relatives called him a jokester who wanted people to feel good. That is the man who never made it home from a bridge crossing at rush hour.
Irvine’s employer issued a brief statement Wednesday as word of the killing spread through the company.
"We are heartbroken by the tragic loss of a member of the Con Edison family in this senseless act of violence. Our deepest condolences go out to his family, friends, colleagues, and everyone who knew and loved him."
Twenty years on the job, overtime shifts, a home in Rockland County, and a commute that should have been routine, that was the life cut short on the span. The person of interest’s surrender gave police someone to question quickly. It did not give Irvine’s children their father back.
Road rage is not a misunderstanding when a round tears through a rear window and a working dad dies in the median. Law-and-order policing means treating bridge gunfire like the life-destroying crime it is, not like traffic with extra noise. A man who clocked in, loved his wife, and made his kids laugh deserved to reach the other side of the bridge.

Con Ed worker fatally shot in GWB road rage incident remembered as hard working Jets fan: ‘Lived for his family 100%’
See more of our coverage in your search results.
The Con Edison worker killed in a road rage-fueled shooting on the George Washington Bridge late Tuesday was a hardworking “family man” who “had so much life,” kin said Wednesday.
Dad of two Koran Irvine, 46, was on his way home from an overtime shift with the energy company when he took a bullet to the right shoulder around 7:15 p.m. Tuesday on the New Jersey-bound upper level of the crossing, according to cops and his family.
“He’s a family man. Has always been a family man, and he lived his life 100% for his family, stayed out of trouble. And I am in disbelief at this point in time,” a cousin told The Post.
“He was a man that lived for his family 100%, the only thing that he loved near and dear to his heart as much as his family was the Jets.”
Irvine, of Valley Cottage, Rockland County, had a son and a daughter – and loved ones admired his relationship with his wife.
“From just their dynamic and how you would experience it in person, you just felt that love in the air,” one relative said. “They really loved each other. They were a special couple.”
“The kids too, they loved their dad and it’s not too long ago they celebrated his birthday.”
Irvine was also a “jokester” who “just always wanted to make people laugh and feel good,” kin said.
“He is always the light of the party,” the relative added. “He had so much life, was very attentive to everyone, always wanted to know people’s needs. He was so inviting.”
He recently lost his mother, but carried the grief with grace, according to the family member.
“Even when his mom passed away a few years ago, he was obviously going through a difficult time, but never made it about himself,” the relative said.
A person of interest was taken into custody less than 24 hours after the deadly violence and was being questioned Wednesday afternoon, the sources said.

sources.news_title: Murder on George Washington Bridge – The Horn News
sources.text:
A 46-year-old man was shot and killed while driving across the George Washington Bridge near the end of the evening rush, snarling traffic for hours on the busy span that connects New York City and New Jersey.
Authorities said that while responding to calls about the shooting on the New Jersey-bound side of the bridge’s upper level just after 7 p.m. Tuesday, they found the man unconscious with a gunshot wound in the driver’s seat of a vehicle.
The man, identified as Koran Irvine of Valley Cottage, New York, was later pronounced dead at a nearby hospital. No arrests have been made, and authorities haven’t given a possible motive for the shooting.
The victim worked for Con Edison, the utility said in a statement, calling the shooting a “senseless act of violence.”
“Our deepest condolences go out to his family, friends, colleagues, and everyone who knew and loved him,” the company said.
Closed lanes reopened about five hours after the shooting, said the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, which operates the bridge.
Opened to traffic in 1931, the iconic, double-decked bridge spans high over the Hudson River, carrying around 100 million vehicles between New Jersey and Manhattan each year, according to the Port Authority, which calls it the world’s busiest. The bridge and its entrances are teeming with cameras.

sources.news_title: Suspect surrenders in road rage shooting slay on NYC George Washington Bridge
sources.text:
A retired NYPD narcotics detective who left the department after he was wounded in an off-duty shooting in 2000 was charged with murder Wednesday for the shooting death of a Con Ed worker during a wild road rage clash on the George Washington Bridge, police officials said.
Victor Romero, 62, who retired from the NYPD 25 years ago, has been identified as the driver of a black Range Rover involved in the slaying on the New Jersey-bound upper level of the Hudson River span about 7:10 p.m. Tuesday, police said.
Cops charged Romero with murder, officials said. His arraignment in Manhattan Criminal Court was pending.
Romero joined the NYPD in 1994, officials said. He retired with a disability pension after he was shot in the wrist and chest during a shootout with three gunmen who tried to rob his family’s Brooklyn laundromat.
Hours after Koran Irvine was shot and killed during a road rage incident on the George Washington Bridge, detectives linked the Range Rover to Romero, who was taken in for questioning without incident.
Romero lives in Haverstraw, N.Y., police said. Detectives were at his home Wednesday evening waiting for a warrant to search his home. Investigators have also recovered the shooter’s gun and Range Rover, although it wasn’t immediately clear where they were found.
On June 25, 2000, Romero was off-duty and had just opened up King’s Laundromat on King’s Highway in East Flatbush when crooks burst in and demanded money around 7 a.m., the Daily News reported at the time.
Romero told them he would hand over the cash and begged them not to shoot anyone, but one of the robbers held a gun to a customer’s cheek, prompting Romero to pull his service weapon and fire eight times.
The crooks shot back. One bullet hit Romero in the wrist and ricocheted, hitting him in the chest. The chest wound was reportedly not serious, but his wrist required reconstructive surgery.
After the shooting, Romero and another employee immediately called 911. ”I’m off duty,” witnesses heard Romero say, according to a report in The New York Times. ”I shot two of them. Help. I’m about to pass out.”
Two of the robbers were each shot in the leg and arrested, while the third got away, according to The News.
Romero had recently celebrated his 11th wedding anniversary at the time of the 2000 shooting, according to reports. He retired from the NYPD with a 3/4 disability pension the following year, a police source said.
Irvine was on his way home from work in his dark blue Volkswagen hatchback when Romero shot him on the Manhattan side of the bridge on the W. 179th St. entrance ramp, officials said. Cops suspect road rage was the motive.
“That’s good to hear,” the victim’s cousin’s 38-year-old husband, who lives in Canarsie, Brooklyn, and declined to give his name, said about the arrest. “We have some family who is law enforcement. They said it’s a high profile case for them. So they were on it and they had footage of the car.”
“I mean we live in New York, right?” he added. “So there’s cameras everywhere, so it’s difficult to get away with anything.”
Irvine was shot in the shoulder and the bullet travelled to his head, police said, but he managed to continue onto the bridge before crashing in the middle of the span. A bullet hole was found in the rear windshield, police sources said.
The killer sped off.
Medics rushed Irvine to Englewood Medical Center in New Jersey, where he died. A longtime resident of Flatbush, Brooklyn, he and his family had recently moved to Valley Cottage in Rockland County, N.Y.

sources.news_title: Person in custody in fatal shooting on George Washington Bridge is retired NYPD officer: sources
sources.text:

The officer was identified as 62-year-old Victor Romero, who retired from the department in 2001.
NYPD detectives tracked down Romero, sources told 1010 WINS, and he is now charged with murder. He is in police custody, and his home in Haverstraw is frozen pending a search warrant.

He was a Con Edison employee from Valley Cottage, Rockland County, officials said. He was not working at the time of his death.

sources.news_title: George Washington Bridge reopens after fatal shooting; no arrests made
sources.text:
A 46-year-old man who was shot while driving along the upper level of the George Washington Bridge Tuesday night has died, according to the NYPD.
The bridge’s westbound upper level, which was closed for hours as police investigated, began reopening just after midnight, according to the Port Authority. All lanes reopened for Wednesday morning’s commute.
The shooting appears to have stemmed from a road rage incident, police said. So far, they have made no arrests and are continuing their investigation.
Police identified the victim as Koran Irvine, of Valley Cottage.
Port Authority police responded to reports of a one-vehicle crash on the bridge’s upper level just after 7 p.m. Tuesday, according to the agency. Officers arrived to find Irvine unconscious and unresponsive with a gunshot wound to the back of his right shoulder, according to the NYPD.
Irvine was taken to Englewood Hospital in New Jersey, where he was pronounced dead.
A Con Edison spokesperson confirmed Irvine had worked for the utility. The company released a short statement saying employees were “heartbroken” and called the shooting a “senseless act of violence.”
The shooting caused major traffic disruptions Tuesday night as authorities shut down travel lanes to investigate. At one point, the Port Authority reported delays of up to 90 minutes on the upper level heading into New York.
The Port Authority reported there were no other injuries.
